_comment: Live deployments on X Layer (chain 196). The delegate address is what users point an EIP-7702 authorisation at, so it is a security-relevant constant: never change it without re-verifying the deployed bytecode against a fresh build of the same source.

supersedes._comment: v1 pinned the sell-side allowance to the swap router. OKX's router does not call transferFrom itself — it reaches tokens through its TokenApprove — so the allowance was never spent and every swap reverted with SwapFailed after the gas was paid. Observed four times on-chain at 223,459 gas each before the cause was found. v2 pins the spender in the grant alongside the router. Grants signed against v1 are unusable and cannot be migrated: the delegate is named in the user's own 7702 authorisation, so it takes a fresh one.

create2._comment: Deployed through the canonical deterministic deployer, so the address is a pure function of the salt and the init code — anyone can recompute it from source and confirm nothing else was deployed here. Verified after deployment: the on-chain runtime code matches a fresh build of src/SarfSessionKey.sol byte for byte.

privileges._comment: Stated explicitly because it is the question anyone auditing this should ask first.
privileges.deployer_retains: nothing — the contract has no privileged role of any kind, so the wallet that paid for deployment has no more power over it than any other address

SarfDelegate.purpose: EIP-7702 delegate for the zap keeper: scoped, per-token-capped exit and re-entry. Nothing can act under it until the account owner sets a scope.
SarfDelegate.status: UNAUDITED - deployed for the passkey proof below. ZAP_7702_ENABLED is false and ZAP_DELEGATE_ADDRESS is unset in production; no user account delegates to it.

passkey_proof.what: registerPasskey, then setScopeWithPasskey verified by X Layer's own RIP-7212 precompile at 0x100, then the same assertion replayed and refused, then revoke() clearing the scope and bumping the epoch.
passkey_proof.why_it_could_not_be_a_test: Foundry's EVM has no P-256 precompile even when forking, so the contract's passkey branch can only meet the real precompile on-chain.
passkey_proof._comment: Every hash above was read back off chain 196 by scanning the deployer's transactions, not recorded from a tool's stdout.

external._comment: Third-party addresses verified present on 196 by direct eth_getCode probe on 2026-08-07.
